authSignInTagline.message: Log masuk dengan akaun sedia ada anda menggunakan mana-mana perkhidmatan di bawah.

authOtherAccountBtn.description: Button on the auth page under a provider this device already signed in with. It reopens that provider's account picker instead of continuing as the account the browser holds. $PROVIDER$ is the provider's name (Google, Apple, ...).

authSignOutAtProviderBtn.message: Akaun $PROVIDER$ salah? Log keluar di sana
authSignOutAtProviderBtn.description: Link on the auth page under a provider that cannot reopen its own account picker (Apple today). Apple ignores an OpenID `prompt`, so a browser already signed in there continues as that account without asking; this is the remedy for that case, not a step before every sign-in - a reader with no session at the provider is asked which account anyway. It opens the provider's account page, where ending the session lives. $PROVIDER$ is the provider's name.

authSigningInKeepOpen.message: Biarkan tab ini terbuka sehingga selesai. Log masuk pertama mengambil masa sedikit lebih lama.

authDoneTagline.message: Anda boleh menutup tab ini dan bertindak balas pada mana-mana halaman yang disokong.

authDoneReturnTagline.message: Anda dibawa kembali ke halaman tadi.

dataConsentBody.message: Emojery menghantar alamat halaman tempat anda bertindak balas, pengecam pemasangan rawak dan token log masuk sekali guna daripada penyedia yang anda pilih; hanya cincangan sehala id akaun anda disimpan. Konteks pilihan kekal dimatikan dalam pelayar ini.

authErrProviderDenied.message: Penyedia tidak melengkapkan log masuk. Cuba lagi atau pilih akaun lain.

authErrEnrollFailed.message: Akaun anda tidak dapat didaftarkan sekarang. Sila cuba lagi seminit lagi.

authErrOutdated.message: Versi Emojery ini sudah lapuk. Kemas kini untuk log masuk.

authErrDeviceLimit.message: Had peranti untuk bulan ini telah dicapai. Sila cuba lagi bulan depan.

deviceLimitHelpLink.description: Link shown beside both device-limit messages (the sign-in refusal and the Account-tab notice). It opens the help article that says what the monthly key limit is, what to do while it holds, and how to reach the operator. Deliberately short: it sits at the end of a sentence that already carries the news.
